citation: Colbert, Elias, and Everett Chamberlin. Chicago and the Great Conflagration. Cincinnati and New York: C. F. Vent; Chicago: J. S. Goodman & Co., 1871.
author: Elias Colbert and Everett Chamberlin
describes_date: Chicago to 1871 and the fire of 8-10 October 1871
repository: Internet Archive, from the Cornell University Library copy (item cu31924028806814)
locator: Crosby's Opera House, pp. 147-148; the fireproof buildings and hotels, p. 151; the Water Tower, pp. 154-155; the drought, pp. 196-197; the South Side's burning, the Tribune building and Potter Palmer's store, pp. 207-210; the night in the cemetery, pp. 265-268; the totals, pp. 287-288; Joseph Medill, pp. 379-380.
rights_note: Published 1871 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3691) in the Internet Archive's plain-text OCR of this scan (cu31924028806814_djvu.txt), at the passages each claim's locator names; quotations are the OCR read as corrected where the machine misread a letter. The page images were not opened.
note: Two Chicago Tribune men writing within weeks of the fire (Colbert was the paper's commercial editor), so period evidence, with the haste of its weeks: it dates the burning of the Tribune building 'at half-past seven in the evening', where the building's own owners describe it standing at daybreak and lost that morning. A different record from colbert_chamberlin_1871_chicago_1833, which is one engraving from the same book.
what_it_supplies: Crosby's Opera House as built (1865, 2,500 seats) and its fall after the Court House
the fall of the Tribune building and of Potter Palmer's marble store leased to Field, Leiter & Co.
thirty thousand people in the old cemetery on Monday night; 17,450 buildings destroyed, 98,500 homeless, more than 250 dead
what_it_does_not_supply: exact times for most of the South Side's buildings
